title: User Permissions & Access Control
short_description: Learn how operating systems and applications represent, combine, analyze, and compare user permissions and access-control configurations using bit manipulation techniques.

real_world_context.problem: An operating system or application needs to efficiently represent, combine, and check user permissions and feature-access configurations. Permissions can be stored as binary masks, where each bit represents whether a particular access right is enabled.
real_world_context.why_it_matters: Bit-based permission systems allow applications to store many access settings compactly and perform permission checks, comparisons, and configuration operations efficiently.

learning_objectives: Understand how user permissions can be represented using binary values and bit masks.
Apply bitwise OR to combine permissions from multiple user roles.
Count set bits to determine the number of enabled permissions.
Use XOR to identify a unique permission or access code.
Understand how a Power Set represents all possible permission configurations.
Apply Maximum XOR techniques to compare permission masks.
Understand how bit manipulation can reduce storage and improve access-control operations.
Choose an appropriate bit manipulation technique based on the type of permission operation being performed.

real_world_mapping.user: Person whose access permissions are being managed
real_world_mapping.user_role: Role containing a predefined set of permissions
real_world_mapping.permission: Individual access right such as read, write, or execute
real_world_mapping.permission_mask: Integer whose bits represent enabled or disabled permissions
real_world_mapping.combined_permissions: Permission mask obtained by combining multiple permission sets
real_world_mapping.enabled_permission: Permission represented by a set bit
real_world_mapping.unique_permission_code: Access code that occurs only once among repeated codes
real_world_mapping.permission_configuration: One possible subset of available permissions
real_world_mapping.permission_difference: Difference between two permission masks represented through XOR

completion_message: You have completed the User Permissions & Access Control mission. You have learned how bit manipulation, set-bit counting, XOR, power sets, and maximum XOR techniques can be applied to represent, combine, analyze, and compare user permissions and access-control configurations efficiently.
